correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the symmetric quadrilateral to a two-parameter lattice normal form using adjacent uniquely selecting primitive width directions and proves those directions form a unimodular basis. The exact gauge then shows that unequal parameters yield only one parallel pair of diameter directions, contradicting the facet-by-facet completeness criterion. The equal positive parameter is exactly the published twisted-square family; the zero endpoint is the published reduced-but-incomplete diamond. Exact rational replay checks the algebraic consequences.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General reduced-polygon structure and general diameter inequalities do not imply the equal-parameter rigidity proved here. The key new implication is that simultaneous completeness eliminates every asymmetric two-parameter normal form.

originality.rationale: The defining 2024 paper gives the twisted squares only as examples, classifies triangles separately, and poses the broader simultaneous reduced/complete problem. The accessible earlier width-minimal classification has a different object class and no completeness condition. Candidate-specific semantic and public searches found no statement exhausting symmetric quadrilaterals by the twisted squares. An older lattice-diameter paper remains a disclosed partial-access risk but uses a different completeness framework according to the defining source.
residual_risks: The full 2001 Bárány–Füredi paper was not accessible for theorem-by-theorem inspection; it uses a different completeness notion according to the defining 2024 source.

Older geometry-of-numbers literature may encode an equivalent classification under different terminology, although the 2024 defining paper cites the main predecessors and still presents the twisted squares only as examples.
The polar involution and exact area/diameter formulas are elementary consequences once the canonical family is established; originality is not claimed for those formulas in isolation.

value.rationale: The defining paper explicitly asks for structure of simultaneously lattice reduced and complete bodies and gives twisted squares as a continuum of planar examples. Classifying the smallest origin-symmetric polygonal class completely is a natural partial answer. The result replaces an example family by an exact moduli classification and supplies a transparent obstruction—loss of a second diameter direction pair—when the two twist coordinates differ.
